facts.claim: The card's `criteria` field (Barkpark.Tasks.Board.to_card, board.ex:216) is `Tasks.criteria_progress(content)` -> defdelegate to Barkpark.Tasks.Criteria.progress/1 (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/criteria.ex:33-41), which computes ONLY %{met: integer, total: integer} by counting entries in content.acceptance_criteria — it never reads or returns any criterion TEXT. This field does NOT need Envelope gating for content (a count is not the protected text), though the existing peek deliberately gates it as a whole unit anyway for consistency (see next fact).

board.ex's next_criterion/1 (defp, ~line 270) and criteria_list/1 (defp, ~line 226-232ish near 'criteria_list' — see criteria_list_cap block right after to_card) BOTH read content['acceptance_criteria'] directly and return the literal 'criterion' TEXT string(s) of entries (next_criterion: first unmet entry's text; criteria_list: up to 8 entries' {text, met}). These ARE task-content fields Envelope.field_readable? would gate — mirroring the merged peek seal, which explicitly guards the equivalent peek_criteria/1 behind readable?.("acceptance_criteria") (board_live.ex:767-773, gated at line 655 via readable?.("acceptance_criteria")) and documents in its own comment (board_live.ex:765-766) that peek_criteria carries 'the data the card's n/m can only count' — i.e. the peek author already drew this exact count-vs-text distinction. So S3's seal must gate BOTH next_criterion and criteria_list (2 field groups off one acceptance_criteria read), and separately gate description_excerpt/design_doc (2 more groups) — NOT the bare `criteria` count. Net: the card projection has (at minimum) description, design_doc, and acceptance_criteria(->criteria_list+next_criterion) as gate-worthy groups; `criteria` (the count) and `labels`/`priority`/`parent_id` mirror the peek's own list of gated fields if parity with the peek is the goal.
